agree.reason: This reader left over price and is happy with the savings; a single $99 visit and a general line that 'every visit is insured' don't justify paying about $25 more on every visit after that, so they probably won't book.

honest.reason: The email turns 'same cleaner every time' into 'your own regular cleaner plus a named backup' and 'you'll always know who's coming', which is true, and every figure it uses is accurate.

works_the_facts.reason: It never puts the price gap as a number ($25 a visit), never says the $99 visit costs $41 less than the apps charge, and gives '1 of 18 left' without setting it against last year's 7 of 18, so the improvement doesn't come through.

right_comparison.reason: The apps appear only as 'cheaper'; the email leaves out that their cleaners are mostly contractors with no insurance on the visit, which is the comparison that would make the higher price make sense.

qualification.reason: The offer has a clear December 31 deadline, and the backup cleaner is tied to sick days and holidays, so the reader can check what the commitment covers.

objections.reason: The price objection is admitted but answered only with facts about Brightway's own staff and no contrast with the apps; the email also leads with a fix for cleaner turnover, which this reader never complained about, and says 'you were right about the cleaners' to someone who didn't raise it.

fit.reason: It's a short email of about 150 words with a subject line and a call to action, but it leaves out the 555-0164 phone number as a second way to book.
